original_question: Let B be a Banach space. Let P be a projection on a finite-dimensional Banach subspace of B. Let L0 + λL be a generator of C0 -semigroup Utλ on B for all λ ∈ [0, λsup ). Let Ut0 leave both PB and its complement (I − P)B invariant, let PLP = 0. Denote Lt ≡ (Ut0 )−1 LUt0 . Let the integrals Z t Z tk−1 dt1 . . . dtk PLt1 . . . Ltk P, k = 1, . . . , n + 1 −∞ −∞ be finite for all t ⩾ 0. If is it possible to find such a λ-dependent operator r n,λ on PB , which is polynomial in λ, and λ-dependent semigroup un,λ t on PB, whose generator is polynomial in λ, such that P(U 0t )−1 U λt P = un,λ t r n,λ + O(λ2n+2 ), λ → +0 λ2 λ2 for all t > 0 ? Let us emphasize that we do not assume here asymptotic behaviour to be uniform in t, it is just assumed for each fixed t > 0. If there are counterexamples, what further restrictions should be assumed to obtain such an asymptotic estimate? Relevance. This problem is important for the derivation of perturbative corrections to Markovian quantum master equations. It seems to be a possible direction of generalization of the classical results by E.B. Davies to higher orders of perturbation theory in λ and seems to be held in a simple example discussed in . It also seems to be necessary for strict perturbative derivation of master equations recently obtained by A.S. Trushechkin .

refined_question: Let B be a real or complex Banach space, let P:B->B be a bounded projection with finite-dimensional range PB, and let \lambda_sup>0. Suppose that for every \lambda in [0,\lambda_sup) the operator L_0+\lambda L generates a C_0-semigroup (U_t^\lambda)_{t\ge 0} on B. Assume that (U_t^0)_{t\ge 0} leaves both PB and (I-P)B invariant, that PLP=0, and that, with L_t := (U_t^0)^{-1} L U_t^0, the iterated operator integrals \int_{-\infty}^t dt_1 \cdots \int_{-\infty}^{t_{k-1}} dt_k\, P L_{t_1}\cdots L_{t_k} P exist as bounded operators on PB for every t>0 and every k=1,\dots,n+1. Is it true that one can find (i) an operator r_{n,\lambda} on PB that is polynomial in \lambda, and (ii) a semigroup (u_{n,\lambda}(t))_{t\ge 0} on PB whose generator is polynomial in \lambda, such that for every fixed t>0 one has P (U^0_{t/\lambda^2})^{-1} U^\lambda_{t/\lambda^2} P = u_{n,\lambda}(t) r_{n,\lambda} + O(\lambda^{2n+2}) as \lambda -> 0+? If not in general, what additional hypotheses on B, L_0, L, or the semigroups are sufficient to guarantee this fixed-time higher-order asymptotic expansion?
justification: The safest paper-faithful refinement I can give is based on the source I could verify directly: your draft reproduces Problem 18 there almost word for word, including the weak-coupling time scaling, the polynomiality requirements in \lambda, and the fixed-time (non-uniform-in-t) remainder statement. Because I could not reliably recover the contents of arXiv:2410.00416 itself through the available web routes, I have not invented a connection to that arXiv paper and instead refined the exact semigroup problem that your draft actually matches.
